text:
nia: rolled NF4 -> FP4 canary to 5% of traffic ~10m ago, seeing ~25% throughput drop and KV cache memory jump on the canary pool :eyes:
nia: tail latency mostly fine but p95/p99 token/sec drops on long contexts
nia: infra telemetry shows per-worker resident memory went from 6GB -> ~18GB on some hosts (KV fragmentation?)
matt: ugh, did we change kernel selection fallback in the last deploy?
jia: we did a kernel selector tweak to prefer the new 4-bit fused kernel for >1k seqs, but it should be faster not worse
carmen: can you paste the profiler traces? nvprof/ncu? :face_with_monocle:
nia: quick ncu snippet (trimmed):
```
==PROF== Kernel: quant_4bit_pack          time: 12.3ms   calls: 1
==PROF== Kernel: attention_fwd            time: 3.9ms    calls: 20
==PROF== Host memcpy H2D                  time: 28.5ms  calls: 7
==PROF== Kernel: quant_dequant_fallback   time: 41.2ms  calls: 7
```
nia: see how `quant_dequant_fallback` dominates on those hosts
samir: fallback kernel looks like it's running on CPU/host path? memcpy H2D high too -> maybe we're moving KV pages back and forth
lex: could be batch heuristic nudging small batches into a 4-bit path that forces dequant->requant for KV merges
matt: any config we changed for `kv_cache_merge_threshold` or the `batching.cutoff_ms`?
jia: we changed `kv_cache_merge_threshold` from 128->64 to reduce fragmentation in most cases, but maybe that causes extra merges for long contexts
carmen: hypothesis: the new fused 4-bit kernel expects packed KV layout; when two different model variants (nf4 vs fp4) get routed, runtime does dequant/pack/unpack which triggers H2D memcpys and host fallback kernels
ops-bot: deploy 1876543000 applied to canary pool (5%) by matt at 2026-03-18T10:05:00Z
nia: repro steps I used: `ab -c 64 -n 5000` with seq=2048 prompt mixture, pinned model -> can reproduce in ~3m
nia: quick mitigation: forcing kernel selection to `legacy-4bit` avoids fallback and drops memory back to 6-7GB, throughput recovers ~20%
samir: can we hot-fix selector to prefer `legacy-4bit` for now and add a telemetry tag to the affected hosts?
matt: I'll push a selector override to the canary and scale to 10% to validate
lex: we've also seen a KV slab fragmentation metric spike (kv_slab_frag_ratio) at the same time, worth correlating
jia: long term: need a unit test that simulates mixed routing (nf4+fp4) to validate pack/unpack code path and measure copies
carmen: also add an NCU flamegraph run on a repro host with `--mixed-variants` so we can prove where the branch goes
matt: rolling selector override now: `runtimectl set-kernel-policy --pool canary --policy prefer=legacy-4bit --until 2026-03-18T12:00:00Z`
ops-bot: kernel policy override applied to pool canary by matt at 2026-03-18T10:07:12Z
nia: after override: memory back down on canary hosts, throughput returned to baseline within two minutes :thumbsup:
jia: good catch. next steps: (1) revert canary deploy or keep but force selector (2) add regression test for mixed-variant KV merge (3) instrument to emit `dequant_requant_count` metric
carmen: I'll open a perf ticket and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml for kernel correctness and selector logic
samir: assigning to `ENG-RUNTIME` sprint this week, priority P0 for rollout rollback if we see user impact
lex: also let's check pinned-client routing rules; customers pinning multiple variants could surface this in prod
matt: thanks everyone. documented repro + mitigation in the ticket. will follow up after the canary reaches 20%
nia: thanks, also added slack alert rule to trigger on memory >12GB for canary pool hosts
jia: adding a small diagnostic dump to runtime when `dequant_requant_count > 0` to capture stack traces
carmen: great. if it reappears, we revert the canary deploy entirely. :white_check_mark:
